svg.text: every amount is Money — never double, never a bare long ✓
the seam — a DB-backed impl is a new class
currency mismatch THROWS — never silently coerced
as long minor: 6 + 1 + 1 == 8, remaining EXACTLY zero ✓
the fix isn't "round more carefully" — it's a type where the invariant is representable
THE ENGINE — three indexes, two critical sections
lost the CAS ⇒ return getTransaction(owner), create nothing
synchronized (txn) — the transaction IS the monitor
append the Refund row — SAME section, cannot diverge
getRefunds(txnId) — O(1) index hit, returns a defensive copy
the lock is PER TRANSACTION — different transactions never contend ✓
charge and refund take the SAME monitor, so status is never read mid-flip ✓
idempotencyKeys is UNBOUNDED — a real leak; TTL or LRU it
the loser of an idempotency race may observe a still-PENDING txn
real gateways answer 409 + retry-after; blocking the loser on the winner's
outbound network call would be worse
synchronized(txn) only works because the registry hands back a
CANONICAL instance — it breaks the day rows come from a DB
CHM = ConcurrentHashMap · the in-memory lock is a single-node artifact
STATE — legality by construction, not by if-checks
refunding a FAILED txn throws BY CONSTRUCTION ✓
the state objects own the BEHAVIOUR.
STRATEGY — one class per payment method (OCP)
stateless · shared · reads the txn, never mutates it
adding Apple Pay = one class + one EnumMap entry ✓
a switch(method) in the gateway would grow a branch per method
the method→processor mapping lives in exactly one place
THE FOUR STUB PROCESSORS — each has a genuinely different rule
CardPaymentProcessor — deterministic issuer decline: any amount whose minor units end in .13 fails
UpiPaymentProcessor — per-transaction cap of 100,000.00 · WalletPaymentProcessor — positive amount only
BankTransferPaymentProcessor — minimum 1.00 · all four are STUBS: no network I/O, which hides partial failure
id · merchantId · customerId · amount: Money · method · createdAt
mutable, but only ever under the gateway's per-transaction monitor
TransactionStatus: PENDING → SUCCESS → REFUNDED, or PENDING → FAILED
one Refund row per refund — the audit trail, written in the same critical section as the total
① PaymentGateway facade → service seam → ② Money FIRST (it makes the invariant expressible) → ③ the engine's three indexes → ④ TransactionState → ⑤ PaymentProcessor strategies

g.text: Patterns: Facade · Strategy (processors) · State (transaction lifecycle) · Flyweight (both singleton sets) · Factory ×2 · Value Object (Money)
Three invariants defended: never double-charge · never refund more than captured · never refund a FAILED or PENDING transaction
Observer (webhooks / receipts) named but NOT built · honest gaps: unbounded idempotency map, stub processors, single-node lock
